cards.title: The item-13 difficulty currency disagrees with itself
cards.detail: pet-island-difficulty.md §5 and slice-1 §4 are in the same currency and disagree. Today one sum banks one unit against a tile costing 1–16. §5 sets easy=2, tricky=3, honeymoon=4; Phase 3 adds mastered=1. Either the cost curve re-bases or session length halves. Run A7 re-bases units ×2 invisibly; this card is the REMAINING question about differential pay. NARROWED 29 Jul, because two thirds of it has been overtaken and only the differential-pay question is left. What is now FALSE: the easy=2/tricky=3/honeymoon=4/mastered=1 tier table describes the DOCUMENT, not the build - nothing difficulty-tiered was ever built, and pay is flat at balance.json pay {item: 2, honeymoon: 3}. What DID ship is a single tier and it is not a difficulty tier at all: the honeymoon pays 3 (balance/index.ts:274-300, deliberately a sibling of itemPay rather than a parameter of it, so a future difficulty tier does not inherit the honeymoon's shape by accident), and overshoot of a pay-2-quantised price now carries forward instead of being zeroed (flow.ts:633-660, commitPlot). So the cost curve did NOT re-base and session length did not halve; the third option happened. WHAT REMAINS OPEN is only this: should a harder item pay more than an easy one? Joe was asked adjacent questions as JT-024 and JT-025 and answered with something else entirely (the reading curriculum, now PB-043), so this has still never been ruled on.

cards.detail: BUILT 28-29 Jul, all three slices shipped and deployed: B1 1cf4e71, B2 ad848e4, B3 9138176. Gates on the A6 signals (ewma >= .85, >= 20 attempts, >= 2 distinct days, no rescue) - harness.ts:184-192, 702-732; probes at 1-in-8 once a rung below reads .75, into their OWN 12-deep ring so an untaught question cannot contaminate the record - harness.ts:180-192, 946, 1127-1132; the universal offer line verbatim with Yes please!/Not now - overlay.ts:701-741, harness.ts:571-578; taking-away introduced by offer off sums 1 alone (JT-020) then dealt MIXED - harness.ts:1152-1165; weakness-lean bounded 65/35 - harness.ts:246-252, 764-780; invisible mercy runs, 3 wrong triggers 2 bottom-rung items, session-local, persists nothing - harness.ts:261-263, 835, 1023-1053; whisper retirement, derived not stored (a rung wakes because its ewma fell, so no flag can disagree with the evidence) - harness.ts:264-267, 546-551, 837-838; "what Auto would do" live - report.ts:243, grownups.ts:447. THE CARD UNDER-DESCRIBED WHAT WAS BUILT, two things it never named: (i) THE HONEYMOON ECONOMY shipped in B2 - a maths item pays 3 instead of 2 during the honeymoon, with a permanently frozen tile index (honeymoonTiles) so the discount can never claw anything back - flow.ts:98, 159, 330, 660 and balance/index.ts:274-300; (ii) LearningDeps.harness became REQUIRED, because the grown-ups panel had been reading a second harness on the wrong clock - grownups.ts:291-301. ONE DIAL IS STILL CONTESTED: whether "bounded 65/35" limits the LEAN or clamps the SHARE is raised as JT-026 and OPEN at time of writing. B3 shipped Fable's reading (a bound on the lean, so a parent's tick always outranks an estimate); if Joe reverses it the fix is a clamp WRAPPING the multiplier, costed at about an hour, and all eight dials sit in one >>> PROVISIONAL block at harness.ts:199-268. cards.title: New animals
cards.detail: Build new sets of animals for the collection in the same style as the existing ones. they should be in sets that go together and should be shown as pages in the album. never all collections in one go, max 5 incomplete collections. new collection opens up when one is completed. collections should be thematically consistent, eg UK garden. Birds, Africa, Ocean, etc. A list with the collections and the animals in them will be provided. STATUS 29 Jul: OPEN, AND THE BRIEF HAS NOW LANDED - docs/pet-island-species-roster.md, 142 lines, ratified rather than draft. It arrived mid-way through the backlog reconciliation (Joe's commit 8189a5e), so this card was OPEN AND UNSPECIFIED for most of the day and is not any more. BUILD TO THE ROSTER, NOT TO A SUMMARY OF IT, including not to this card - read it in full first. His one-sentence acceptance test still governs and does not depend on the roster: 'i cannot run out of animal rewards' - the supply must not be exhaustible by a child who keeps playing. WHAT THE ROSTER SETTLES, in brief and only as a pointer: ~296 new builds across 20 collections on top of the live base 24, explicitly NOT a build order - collections ship ONE AT A TIME on the existing 85% unlock cadence, so do not attempt the roster in one run and do not let the scale tempt anyone into generating species in bulk without review. KITS BEFORE SPECIES is the architecture and the whole leverage: six kits (quadruped, songbird, raptor, swim, minibeast, bespoke), built once, after which a species is DATA - proportions, palette, two or three detail parts. THE LIVE 24 ARE FROZEN: never rebuilt, never restyled, though their geometry is fair game as a starting point. Roster 6 carries Joe's OWN open questions (ship order, whether Prehistoric ships at all, IUCN wording) - those are his, to be raised in the workbench when they block, and NOT to be settled with Fable. WHAT IS MEASURED TODAY, so the brief can be read against it rather than re-derived. THE SUPPLY IS FINITE AND ITS SIZE IS 600: pets.ts:20-26 SPECIES is a fixed 24-entry list of Kenney GLB basenames, sets.ts:105-145 SETS is 25 (1 natural + 12 solid + 12 stripy; the spotted twelve were dropped because the texture cannot carry dots, and the legendary ten are PB-029), and sets.ts:160 totalVariants = 25 x 24 = 600. So it is 600, not the brief's ~1,000. Stale comment to fix while you are there: main.ts:420-422 and :1185 still say '19 candidates' and 'one time in 19' against a 24-entry SPECIES. TWO EXPENSIVE FACTS FROM HANDOFF 6 THAT CONSTRAIN ANY DESIGN: a set is ONE RECOLOURED ATLAS, not a per-variant texture, because every species shares a single material (atlas.ts:111-166, cache key setId/speciesId); and set textures are CACHED AND DETACHED, NEVER DISPOSED, because disposing one breaks every pet of that set including ones she already owns (brief 19). THE NAMING QUESTION IS NOW ANSWERED BY THE ROSTER, AND THE ANSWER CARRIES A BRIEF-19 TRAP - this is the first thing to get right, ahead of any species work. Roster 3 replaces today's behaviour: the given name becomes the alien-word generator SEEDED DETERMINISTICALLY FROM species + set, so every child's blue-set hedgehog is the same Bimo forever, plus a real fixed species name as 'playground currency'. Names are generated once, audited, and frozen AS DATA - never regenerated, or the shared bond breaks. THE TRAP: PET NAMES TODAY ARE PROCEDURALLY GENERATED PER HATCH FROM UNSEEDED Math.random - petName(defaultRng) at main.ts:1167, defaultRng = Math.random at core/rng.ts:5 - and the name never sees the species or the set, so two children get different names for the same lion. It IS persisted once drawn (flow.ts:311-312 bakes it into the Pet record, save.ts:171/226 round-trips it), so nothing is lost on reload. But sets.ts:13-16 and :162-168 already DECLARE the opposite intent - 'Names are fixed per variant and graded by set (brief 5, voice.md 2)', with variantKey documented as 'Used for the name table' - and that name table does not exist anywhere in the code. Whether the brief keeps procedural naming or replaces it with the fixed per-variant table sets.ts already assumes is a genuine open question, so JUNO ALREADY OWNS PETS WHOSE NAMES WERE DRAWN RANDOMLY, and a naive switch to deterministic naming RENAMES THE CREATURES SHE HAS ALREADY HATCHED. That is a brief 19 violation - nothing she owns is ever lost, and a pet's name is the most personal thing she owns. JOE HAS SINCE ANSWERED THIS AND HIS ANSWER IS SIMPLER THAN A MIGRATION LAYER (c54e286, 29 Jul): 'i will give you juno's already achieved animal's names as her latest save game later, you can swap the first hard code out after.' So HER EXISTING PETS' NAMES BECOME THE CANONICAL DETERMINISTIC NAMES for those species+set pairs - pinned as data in the frozen name table, not migrated around. Nothing of hers changes, and the table is right for every other child too, because the table IS the source of truth. What follows for the build: the name table must be DATA WITH PINNABLE ENTRIES FROM DAY ONE, so a supplied name overrides a generated one for a given species+set - that is the seam her save plugs into; a TEMPORARY HARDCODE IS EXPLICITLY SANCTIONED until her save arrives ('swap the first hard code out after'), and it must be marked unmistakably as >>> PROVISIONAL with the exact lines named in the handoff; DO NOT BUILD A GENERAL RENAME-MIGRATION MECHANISM - it is not needed and would be a large risky thing built for a case that will not occur; still write the 19 test (hatch under the old scheme, move to the new, assert the old pet is untouched), and because the id EMBEDS the name (flow.ts:311-312, id 'pet'+n+'-'+name) check what an id migration would touch before assuming either path is safe. HER SAVE HAS NOT ARRIVED YET: do not invent her pets' names to fill the table, exactly as you must not invent species. Leave the pins empty and obvious. Note also that sets.ts:13-16 and :162-168 already ANTICIPATED this - 'Names are fixed per variant and graded by set (brief 5, voice.md 2)', with variantKey documented as 'Used for the name table' - so the roster is ratifying an intent the code has carried unimplemented all along. THE AUDIT IS JOE'S MANUAL WORK AND IT IS LARGE: every generated name needs checking for pronunciation and for real-word or rude-word collisions, and name audio is baked in Olivia's voice. The audit surface is therefore a FIRST-CLASS DELIVERABLE, not a byproduct. HIS REVIEW WILL LIKELY HAPPEN OUTSIDE THE DRUMBEAT, in a session of his own ('lots of manual review work that i may do in a separate session'), so the review surface must be resumable, must not need a manager running, and must not be a wall of prose - it belongs in the workbench in reviewable units, the way joe/noun-candidates.json and joe/pairs-audit.json already work (JT-004 and JT-005 are the pattern to read before designing it).

cards.title: Fred-talk has no way in
cards.detail: Joe, ruling JT-008(2): 'we have no fred talk set up, open a card for that.' He is right, and the machinery is not the missing part — build.ts still has fredTalk(), FRED_SOUNDS and a fred() handle, and A2 now reports it through onHelp('fred'). What is missing is any affordance that reaches it: the overlay wires 'say it again' and nothing else, and the mash rescue was deliberately changed to say the whole word slowly instead (build.ts header, product owner's call: TTS stop consonants bark). So the code path is live and unreachable. Two halves to decide together: (a) the WAY IN, which Run C already specs as the second step of the hint ladder ('Fred, show me?'), so building a button now may be building it twice; (b) the VOICE, which is JT-006 - the 43 recorded phonemes are what make sounding-out pleasant rather than merely available. cards.title: A7 regression: the reading page mix quietly doubled the find pages
cards.detail: Found while surveying A3's deal path, not yet fixed. main.ts passes state.readProgress to dealReading as the PAGE INDEX, and deal.ts:69 asks pageKind(page), which is mix[page % 4] over ['find','build','build','build']. Since A7 readProgress counts UNITS and advances by pay.item = 2 per page, so the index goes 0,2,4,6 and the mix reads find,build,find,build - one find page in two, where the data says one in four. Demonstrated: pre-A7 'find build build build find build' vs today 'find build find build find build'. This is exactly the trap A7's own field note names ('anything asserting pacing should ask in items, or it is asserting the denomination instead'); the month-walk pinned COSTS in items and the page mix was never asked. Fix is at the deal path, not in balance.json - the index wants converting from units to items (readProgress / itemPay(), exact because a reading page pays exactly one item) - and it needs a test that pins the mix a child actually SEES across an egg, since the existing balance.test.ts pins pageKind(0..3) directly and cannot see this. Note before changing it: alternating find/build may well be the nicer mix. The bug is that nobody chose it. CLOSED 28 Jul with A3. Joe ruled it (JT-010(2)): 'reading mix should be 3 build, 1 find. period.' The data was right all along; balance.pagesRead() converts units to pages at the deal path, and the new tests in balance.test.ts walk readProgress the way the game moves it instead of asking pageKind(0..3) directly - which is why the old suite could not see it.

cards.title: Egg/Tile balance

BUILT 29 Jul (29bb22b), and SUPERSEDED IN MECHANISM by PB-042/JT-012: the unbound end is now bound, but as a PRICE rather than a stop. Both ends are one corridor in balance.json governor.corridor - crowded 1.5 tiles per pet (Joe's 3-tiles-vs-2-animals, unchanged) and empty 3.0 tiles per pet (the maths-push end) - balance/index.ts:68-75, governors.ts:179-196, 299. So the sentence "i dont think we have bound properly" is no longer true. One thing shipped that this card never asked for and a future reader should not mistake for drift: a GRACE PERIOD suspends both walls until pets >= 5 AND tiles >= 10 (JT-016), so Fred cannot mention crowding to a child with five animals - balance.json governor.grace, balance/index.ts:36-45.

cards.title: A page she abandons is re-measured when she re-does it
cards.detail: A consequence of JT-009(c), recorded rather than fixed, because fixing it costs more than it does. She finds 11 of 12 words, taps X, and comes back to the same page whole - so those 11 words are answered TWICE and emitted twice, and the second pass is easier by construction because she has just done them. Abandonment therefore nudges accuracy UP a little. Why it is small: the latency ring is 30 deep and the EWMA alpha is .15, so a handful of repeats move nothing you can see, and it needs a child who actually leaves pages mid-way to appear at all. Why it is not fixed: de-duplicating attempts per card would mean the tally knowing what a CARD is - which store it came from, whether it is the same one - and attempts.ts was deliberately split out of the overlay to keep it arithmetic over an event order rather than a thing that knows about ReadPick. The honest cheap alternative if it ever matters is to mark the repeat rather than drop it: challengeFailed already sets readHeld, so the overlay knows on the way back IN that this page is a re-visit, and one bit on AttemptEvent would let A6 decide. Trigger: if the grown-ups report ever reads flattering for a child who leaves a lot, look here first. STILL OPEN AND STILL RIGHT after Run B - attempts.ts:39-53 still carries only kind/index/correct/latency with no repeat bit, and EWMA_ALPHA is still .15 (harness.ts:182). But the 'moves nothing you can see' estimate was made BEFORE Run B, and Run B added three new consumers of the same attempt stream: the probe ring, the mercy counter and the weakness lean (harness.ts:1036-1053, 1086). A duplicated attempt now also feeds the mercy trigger, which fires on a run of three - a much shorter window than a 30-deep ring - so the effect is no longer purely diluted. Re-estimate the size before deciding it is still too small to fix.

cards.title: Resume a paused find page where she left it (JT-009 reading b, parked)
cards.detail: Parked by Joe's own ruling, not rejected: 'we go with (c) nothing changes, she does the page again. if it flags in play test, i will bring it back.' This card is the bring-it-back. THE CASE: a find page grows from 3 words to 12, so a girl who finds 11 and taps X re-finds all 11 to get paid. Under (c) that is a chore rather than a punishment, and the bet is that it stays a chore at 12 words. Play-test signal that the bet lost: she stops leaving pages she is finding hard because leaving is expensive, or she leaves and does not come back to the egg at all. WHAT IT WOULD COST, surveyed at the time so a future run does not survey it twice: in-session round state (which targets were found), a change to the ported wordFind renderer to mount with some already struck - which is a PARITY question against tools/smoke/parity.mjs rather than a free one - and nothing at all in the economy, which is what made it the cheapest of the two live alternatives. Reading (a), pro-rata, is NOT parked here: it needs part-items in a currency A7 just re-based to whole ones and it moves pages-per-egg, which the month-walk pins. If (c) ever fails, (b) is the one to build.

cards.title: The governors say 'invitation' and behave like a refusal
cards.progress: SPLIT IN TWO by manager run 1, because Joe reported it live: the deployed build was 'erroneously forcing tile building' with Juno frustrated by it. HALF A, THE OVERRIDE, IS SHIPPED AND DEPLOYED (58425b6): invite() now returns 'asked' | 'again', the first tap on a paused egg or socket spends itself on Fred's line, and the very next tap on the same thing opens the round regardless. Fred's memory clears ON the override, so every override is preceded by the announcement and none is a silent wave-through. Verified in the live bundle at https://jtr31415.github.io/JunosIsland/. HALF B, THE ESCALATING PRICE, IS NOW SHIPPED AND DEPLOYED TOO (bdc9290, f0de911, f38cf60, ratified in ad848e4) - manager run 4 built it after Joe answered JT-013 through JT-019, and runs 5-6 shipped over it unchanged. Live at balance.json governor.escalation (slope .25, capMultiple 3) with the curve at balance/index.ts:520-532 and the step counters at governors.ts:355-368; the announcement before every rise is Fred's ask itself - governors.ts:277-283, 340-344. THE CARD'S OWN PREMISE IS NOW STALE IN ONE PLACE: balance.json no longer HAS a tilesPerPet field. It was replaced by the corridor {crowded 1.5, empty 3.0} with 2.0 as an unstored target - balance/index.ts:47-79 - so anything below that reads tilesPerPet is describing a file that has moved on. TWO PAIRS OF WALLS NOW EXIST AND ARE EASY TO CONFUSE: the WARNING walls (1.5 / 3.0, where Fred speaks) and the PRICE walls (1.2 / 4.0, where it starts costing more), which JT-014 asked for and JT-021 marked PROVISIONAL pending play-test - balance.json governor.__jt021 carries that marker deliberately so it is findable. The three numbers the card demanded were settled as: (1) 2.0 tiles per pet is the target and the shipped 1.5 survives as the crowded wall, because Joe's own 'buffer to 2:3' IS 1.5 tiles per pet - he re-filed his morning number as the edge in the same sentence that set the new centre; (2) the walls are 1.5 and 3.0 tiles per pet, symmetric in ANIMALS-PER-TILE (2/3, 1/2, 1/3 evenly spaced), which is the unit Joe stated his target in and why they are not symmetric in tiles-per-pet; (3) the escalation is linear, 1 + d/4 per whole step past the wall, capped at 3x, applied to the exact curve value BEFORE the round-to-a-multiple-of-two - about 38 sums at one past, 54 at three past, 96 absolute maximum. TWO THINGS NEEDED JOE before half B was safe to ship, and BOTH ARE ANSWERED - they were migrated out of the retired DECISIONS-FOR-JOE.md into the workbench and closed there (dd2ed72). The corridor question became JT-018 ('reading should be more expensive... i have an unlimited amount of tiles but a limited stash of animals as rewards. neither must ever run out') and JT-021 ('lets keep for now, its very hard to predict and depends on play test. mark it in the code commentary so we find it easy if we need to change'), which is why the price walls carry the __jt021 marker; the second became JT-019, answered 'we get fred to tell her how many she needs to restore balance', and JT-022 accepted the grace period's consequence that Fred can never mention crowding below six animals. ONE THREAD STILL DANGLES, and nothing is blocked on it: JT-019's answer means Fred counts out loud, so twenty numerals want recording - that is JT-023, still OPEN in the workbench. The splice points already exist in data (voice/scripts.json:59 idPrefix 'count.', templates at :92 and :93) and there is no src-side consumer, so the lines speak through Web Speech today and will keep working if the recordings never arrive.
cards.detail: Raised by Joe, 28 July, correcting a claim made in session: "there is currently a hard bound. if there are not enough tiles for the number of animals, it says 'they need more homes' and wont let you do an egg. same probably applies the other way round." He is right, and it applies both ways. THE GAP between the doctrine and the behaviour: governors.ts:8-14 states "They are INVITATIONS, never lockouts. Nothing greys out; Fred asks for the other thing instead, and the child may ignore him." The first half is true and the second is not. interactions.ts:82-89 (egg) and :140-141 (socket) call invite() and return the flow UNCHANGED - the round never opens. So nothing greys out, the tap can be repeated forever and nothing already earned is taken away, but she cannot actually do the thing she asked for. 'The child may ignore him' is precisely what she cannot do. That is a lockout with a warm line on it. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: brief 19 is the rule the whole project bends to - invitations never lockouts, nothing expires, nothing is taken back - and a doctrine comment that misdescribes its own code is how a future change gets justified by a rule it does not actually follow. PB-039 does NOT fix this; it moves WHEN the stop fires (the maths-push end from ~1.2 tiles per animal out to 3 animals per 2 tiles, so she meets it far less often) and leaves the mechanism alone. THREE WAYS TO CLOSE IT, Joe's call. (a) MAKE THE CODE MATCH THE DOCTRINE: Fred asks, and if she taps again the round opens anyway - the ask becomes real and she may override it. Softest, and the truest to brief 19. (b) MAKE THE DOCTRINE MATCH THE CODE: keep the hard stop, rewrite the comment to say so honestly - a bound the child cannot cross is a legitimate design, it is just not an invitation. (c) SPLIT THEM: the ratio corridor is a genuine stop, the break-watch stays an invitation, and the doctrine distinguishes the two kinds. Nothing should be built here until he picks one, because (a) and (b) are opposite answers to the same sentence. ANSWERED by Joe, 28 July (JT-012), and it is none of the three cleanly - it is (a) with a fourth thing behind it: "tough one. it should start with invitation first, the let the user run with whatever they want to do up to a point otherwise we risk breaking the balance of the island. we then make the reward really really tough to reach the reward if it pushes imbalance further if its too far out of balance. with an announcement. match this to PB-042 when we pick it up. target ratio i think should be 1 animal per 2 tiles, with a buffer to 2:3 either way, then it starts to become increasingly tougher to get either." So the stop is replaced by a PRICE. Invitation first and she may override it; past the buffer the thing she is over-buying gets progressively dearer rather than refused, announced so it is never a silent tax. Nothing is ever taken away, which keeps brief 19, and the island cannot be broken, which is what the hard stop was protecting. BUILD IS EXPLICITLY HELD by Joe ("hold build until we pick up PBI#42") - this card is where it gets picked up. THREE THINGS THE BUILD WILL NEED SETTLING FIRST, all numeric. (1) His target here is ONE ANIMAL PER TWO TILES - 2.0 tiles per animal - which is NOT what the code holds: balance.json's tilesPerPet is 1.5, three tiles per two animals, his own earlier ruling of 28 July. PB-039 shipped against 1.5. Whether 2.0 supersedes 1.5 or describes the far end of the new buffer is the first question. (2) 'a buffer to 2:3 either way' needs pinning as two ratios; 2:3 either side of a 1:2 target is not symmetric in tiles-per-pet and the two walls have to be written out as numbers before anything is coded. (3) The escalation curve: how much dearer, over what distance, and does it cap. Note the cost curves are the WRONG place to look for the equilibrium itself - 17ad266 established that egg and tile are the same curve to within rounding - but a deliberate divergence between them is precisely the mechanism this ruling asks for, which is the first time that has been true.

cards.title: The reading progression curriculum
cards.detail: RAISED BY JOE HIMSELF, 29 Jul, and it arrived on the wrong card - it is the note he closed ruling JT-025 with, so it would have been lost inside a closed ruling if it did not become a card. His words, in full: 'we need to catch up here with the reading progression curriculum. 1. adding nouns 2. finding word challenge with only similar words. 3. 5-letter longer non-noun words, etc etc.' WHY IT EXISTS: B2 shipped a honeymoon that makes MATHS cheaper only, while the offer she hears promises 'eggs and tiles faster'. Joe was asked whether to reword the promise and answered JT-024 with 'see answer to JT-025' - so he did NOT reverse B2 and nothing is to be reverted; his fix is to build the reading side until the promise becomes true. THIS IS A SURVEY-THEN-ASK CARD, NOT A BUILD-TO-SPEC ONE. His three rungs are a sketch and his own 'etc etc' says so. Reading already has real machinery (src/challenges/wordFind, the noun lists in joe/) and the maths ladder PB-030 is the worked precedent, so the job is to map what exists against his three rungs and hand him the questions the sketch leaves open. WHAT PB-030 PROVED IS GENERAL AND SHOULD BE COPIED: selection lives in the island layer and never in src/core/, because golden.json pins per-level generator behaviour and parity.mjs drives v0's own level switch, so the two regression gates constrain a ladder from opposite directions; nothing demotes, ever, and the cheapest way to honour that is to make regression EMERGENT from the estimate rather than a stored flag; one offer a session, and a decline costs nothing but a cooldown; a capability tick is a parent's statement and must always outrank an estimate; probes go into their own ring. WHAT IS SPECIFIC TO MATHS AND MUST NOT BE COPIED BLINDLY: (a) the one-pool, share-follows-tick-count model exists because maths has exactly TWO peer paths, whereas reading's build/find split is already governed by a FIXED 3-build-1-find mix Joe ruled in JT-010(2) - so a weakness lean in reading would collide with that ruling the same way B3's lean collided with JT-010(1). Expect that conflict and raise it early. (b) pagesRead derives the reading page by dividing progress by the pay rate, so reading's difficulty and reading's economy are coupled in a way maths's are not; B2 already hit this. (c) the promotion constants (ewma >= .85, >= 20 attempts, >= 2 distinct days) are calibrated to SHORT maths items and must be re-derived, not inherited, for items that take much longer. AND THE LESSON THAT SAVED B3: check each spec clause against joe/tasks.json before building it. Run A's spec paragraphs are dense and were written before Joe's rulings existed.

cards.title: An abandoned tile follows her around, and hijacks every later tap
cards.detail: LIVE BUG, reported by Joe on 29 July from Juno playing the deployed build: "if a tile has been started and then abandoned, then tapping any tile jumps back into the building of the same tile, frustrating for her if she tries to tap an animal." The symptom that matters is the last clause - she taps an ANIMAL and gets dropped back into building a tile she had walked away from. THE RULING IS JOE'S AND IS SETTLED, so it is not to be redesigned: "if she abandons a tile, the progress towards reward is saved, the location and type is not. so when she then taps another glowing tile to build one, progress picks up but location and type is rechosen by her on entry." Three parts. (1) Abandoning KEEPS her progress toward the reward - she earned it and brief 19 makes that non-negotiable. (2) Abandoning DISCARDS the location and the type - neither was ever a commitment. (3) Her next tap on any glowing socket starts a build THERE, in a type she chooses ON ENTRY, carrying the saved progress. WHERE IT LIVES: askForLand today RESUMES a standing plot, and that resumption is the reported behaviour. The machinery is src/island/plot.ts (lifecycle behind ports), flow.plot, and props.adopt. READ docs/HANDOFF.md FIRST - three separate faults have already been in this exact seam (the dead-on-arrival plot, the plot stranded on a closed panel, and the plot that showed her last week's answer) and none was visible to the unit tests on either side, because the plot builds whatever it is told and the flow records whatever is chosen. Only a test driving the plot AND the flow together catches this class; tests/island/plot.test.ts is the precedent. Verify against the real tap path in interactions.ts rather than the flow alone, and check what a socket tap does when there is no standing plot at all, because that path changes too. ONE DETAIL NOBODY HAS RULED ON, and it is what she will actually see: whatever had already GROWN on the abandoned plot is discarded visually when she rechooses the type, while the sums count carries over. That follows from Joe's rule, but it is the visible half, so it is worth his eye on the tablet once it ships.
